summary: The article evaluates linear representation steering on single-letter identifier declaration tasks across Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen2.5-14B. By extracting a 25-dimensional subspace using ridge regression on calibration token states, the intervention achieves 100% preference reversal across 512 test pairs while matching-norm random directions achieve zero. The methodology is well-isolated and clearly documented, though limited to a highly constrained single-token synthetic setup.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including both full-vector positive controls and norm-matched orthogonalized Gaussian negative controls.
Precise specification of experimental parameters, including model revisions, layer cutoffs, ridge penalty hyperparameters, and test sample index splits.
Clear grounding in linear algebra (extracting 25 independent contrasts from 26 letter indicators) applied to activation steering.
Comprehensive disclosure of hardware, runtime environment, and dependency versions.
weaknesses: Narrow benchmark scope restricted to single-letter declaration tokens with immediate 1:1 token alignment.
No exploration of layer sensitivity or how intervention effectiveness varies across different depths of the network.
Lacks evaluation on multi-token identifiers or natural programming language variable renamings.
suggestions: Extend the benchmark across multiple intermediate layers to map the persistence and formation of the identifier subspace through the residual stream.
Evaluate multi-character identifier tokens to determine how well linear subspace projection scales beyond isolated single-letter contrasts.
Include evaluations on transferability of the fitted subspace between different base model checkpoints.

claims.text: The frozen checkpoints are Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base revision 0396a76181e127dfc13e5c5ec48a8cee09938b02 and Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B base revision 97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9.
We read the declaration token after block 6 of 28 in the 7B model (width 3,584) and after block 10 of 48 in the 14B model (width 5,120).
Twenty-six class indicators have at most 25 independent contrasts here.
